Task: furnish this empty bedroom (Turkish: YATAK ODASI, ÇOCUK ODASI = children's room, EBEVEYN YATAK ODASI = master bedroom) labelled 'Çocuk Odası' on the plan. Style brief: Scandinavian, light oak floor, white walls, linen textiles, warm daylight.

Room (metres, X right, Y up):
{"room_id": "r_L1_cocuk_odasi", "label": "Çocuk Odası", "room_type": "bedroom", "area_m2": 10.8, "polygon_m": [[0.25, 4.25], [4.25, 4.25], [4.25, 6.95], [0.25, 6.95]], "doors": [{"id": "d_L1_002", "center": [4.3, 5.5], "width": 0.8, "opens_into_this_room": true}], "windows": [{"id": "win_L1_004", "center": [2.25, 7.08], "width": 1.2, "sill_height": null}]}

Allowed types with their size options [width, depth]:
- bed_double: height 0.5 m, size options [1.4, 2.0], [1.6, 2.0], [1.8, 2.0] (usually against a wall)
- bed_single: height 0.5 m, size options [0.9, 1.9], [0.9, 2.0], [1.2, 2.0] (usually against a wall)
- nightstand: height 0.5 m, size options [0.4, 0.4], [0.5, 0.4], [0.6, 0.45]
- wardrobe: height 2.1 m, size options [1.2, 0.6], [1.8, 0.6], [2.4, 0.6] (usually against a wall)
- dresser: height 0.8 m, size options [1.0, 0.45], [1.2, 0.5], [1.4, 0.5] (usually against a wall)
- desk: height 0.75 m, size options [1.2, 0.6], [1.4, 0.7], [1.6, 0.8] (usually against a wall)
- chair: height 0.9 m, size options [0.4, 0.4], [0.45, 0.45], [0.5, 0.5]
- bookshelf: height 1.8 m, size options [0.8, 0.3], [1.0, 0.35], [1.2, 0.4] (usually against a wall)
- armchair: height 0.85 m, size options [0.8, 0.8], [0.9, 0.9], [1.0, 1.0]
- bench: height 0.45 m, size options [1.0, 0.4], [1.2, 0.4], [1.4, 0.45]
- ottoman: height 0.45 m, size options [0.5, 0.5], [0.6, 0.6], [0.8, 0.8]
- office_chair: height 1.0 m, size options [0.55, 0.55], [0.6, 0.6], [0.65, 0.65]

Rules that are checked afterwards (pieces that fail are moved or removed):
- every footprint lies fully inside the room polygon; pieces do not overlap;
- keep 0.6 m free in front of beds, sofas, desks and wardrobes (front = the -Y side at rotation 0, rotated with the piece);
- keep a 0.9 m wide walkway from every door to every other door and window;
- keep the door swing free: a half circle with the door width as radius inside the room the door opens into, and 0.6 m in front of every door;
- within 0.3 m of a window nothing may be taller than the sill (sill_height null = 0.9 m assumed); beds, sofas and tables may stand under a window;
- a piece with against_wall true must touch a wall with its back edge (its +Y side at rotation 0): choose rotation_deg so the back faces the wall (0 = back to a wall on the +Y side, 90 = back to a wall on the -X side, 180 = back to a wall on the -Y side, 270 = back to a wall on the +X side) and set the centre half the depth away from the wall.

A good layout for this room type: one bed (bed_double for a master bedroom, bed_single, bunk_bed or crib for a children's room) with the headboard against a wall and not under the door, a nightstand on each free side of a double bed, one wardrobe against a wall, optionally a desk with an office_chair.

Fields of the answer: pieces, a list (at most 12, the most important piece first) of objects with
- type: one of bed_double, bed_single, nightstand, wardrobe, dresser, desk, chair, bookshelf, armchair, bench, ottoman, office_chair
- center: [x, y] of the footprint centre in metres, in the same frame as the room polygon
- rotation_deg: 0..360 counter-clockwise; at 0 the width runs along X and the front faces -Y
- size: [width, depth] in metres, exactly one of the size options of the type
- against_wall: true when the back edge touches a wall
- reason: one short sentence why the piece is there

Answer only with JSON.
